He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Ohio Bobcats men's basketball|Ohio Bobcats]] and has represented the [[Senegal national basketball team|Senegalese national team]], where he participated in the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2014/player/Maurice-Ndour|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140831074228/http://www.fiba.com/basketballworldcup/2014/Maurice-Daly-NDOUR|url-status=live|archive-date=August 31, 2014|title=Maurice NDOUR|work=FIBA.com|accessdate=August 30, 2014}} ==Early life== Ndour, a Senegalese native, was born in Sindia and raised in [[M'Bour]] where he played soccer and basketball as a youth. During his teenage years, he was noticed playing in a local basketball tournament and was asked if he'd like to play high school basketball in Japan. For his sophomore, junior and senior years, Ndour attended Okayama Gakugeikan High School where he was an all-Okayama MVP honoree and all-star selection in 2009 and 2010.{{cite web|last=Alexander|first=Elton |url=http://www.cleveland.com/sports/college/index.ssf/2013/11/ohio_university_basketball_pla.html|title=Ohio University basketball player Maurice N'dour is not a typical transfer|work=Cleveland.com|date=November 7, 2013|accessdate=July 16, 2015}}{{cite web|url=http://www.ohiobobcats.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/maurice_ndour_851444.html|title=Maurice Ndour Bio|work=OhioBobcats.com|accessdate=July 16, 2015|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150716170444/http://www.ohiobobcats.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/maurice_ndour_851444.html|archivedate=July 16, 2015}} ==College career== After graduating from Okayama Gakugeikan in 2011, Ndour moved to the United States where he enrolled at [[Monroe College]] and played two seasons for the Mustangs. He was a two-time NJCAA All-Region selection and finished his two-year career at Monroe with 848 points, placing him eighth on the all-time Mustang scoring list. He averaged 9.4 points, 6.4 rebounds and 2.4 blocks per game as a freshman in 2011–12, and 16.2 points, 10.5 rebounds and 2.3 blocks per game as a sophomore in 2012–13. In 2013, Ndour transferred to [[Ohio University]] where he spent his final two college seasons playing for the [[Ohio Bobcats men's basketball|Bobcats]]. As a junior in [[2013–14 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team|2013–14]], he averaged 13.8 points and 7.0 rebounds in 36 games, and earned second-team All-[[Mid-American Conference]] and NABC All-District 14 second team honors. As a senior in [[2014–15 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team|2014–15]], he again earned second-team All-MAC honors after averaging 16.0 points, 8.3 rebounds and 2.3 blocks per game.{{cite web |url=http://stats.washingtonpost.com/cbk/players.asp?id=121537|title=#5 Maurice Ndour|work=WashingtonPost.com|accessdate=July 16, 2015}} ==Professional career== ===Dallas Mavericks (2015)=== After going undrafted in the [[2015 NBA draft]], Ndour joined the [[New York Knicks]] for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/sl15/knicks-summer-league-roster-announced|title=Knicks Summer League Roster Announced|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2015|accessdate=July 16, 2015}} On July 23, 2015, Ndour signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite news|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavs-sign-maurice-ndour/|title=Mavs sign Maurice Ndour|work=Mavs.com|date=July 23, 2015|accessdate=July 23, 2015}} He appeared in the team's first four preseason games but missed the final three games of the preseason schedule with a left tibial stress reaction. He was subsequently waived by the Mavericks on October 26 prior to the start of the regular season.{{cite news|last=Charania|first=Shams|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/sources--mavericks-waive-maurice-ndour-to-finalize-roster-194039250.html|title=Sources: Mavericks waive Maurice Ndour to finalize roster|work=Yahoo.com|date=October 26, 2015|accessdate=October 26, 2015}} ===Real Madrid (2015–2016)=== On December 5, 2015, Ndour signed a one-year deal with [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]].{{cite news|title=Official Announcement: Maurice Ndour|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/12/official-announcement-maurice-ndour|work=RealMadrid.com|date=December 5, 2015|accessdate=December 5, 2015}}{{cite news|title=Maurice Ndour: new Real Madrid player|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/12/maurice-ndour-new-real-madrid-player|work=RealMadrid.com|date=December 5, 2015|accessdate=December 5, 2015}} In 12 [[Liga ACB|league]] games for the club, he averaged 2.3 points and 1.8 rebounds per game. He also appeared in six [[EuroLeague]] games, averaging 1.7 points and 1.2 rebounds per game. ===New York Knicks (2016–2017)=== On July 14, 2016, Ndour signed with the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite 2016, recording three points, two rebounds and one steal off the bench in a 102–89 loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899500|title=Knicks vs.
